dedupe_keys.name: firecom austin real time urban fire and smoke tracking digital twin with a public dashboard

description: This case study presents FireCom, a digital twin built in Austin, Texas, to track and predict smoke from urban fires in real time and share it with responders and residents. Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin's Urban Information Lab, working with the City of Austin, fused air quality sensor readings, weather data and a 3D model of the city, so that the platform reflects how buildings channel smoke and how many people are exposed in dense areas, which regional wildfire tools do not handle. Results are shown on a publicly accessible dashboard intended for both emergency response and public awareness, and the authors offer the design as a scalable framework other cities can copy. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY in Computational Urban Science (2025), with full text in Europe PMC. Coverage is the city of Austin. Caveats: an exploratory case study; the dashboard address and any code are not given in the abstract, and the facts here come from the abstract. Simulation uses: a pattern for coupling fire and smoke models with live sensors in a city digital twin for fire services, and exposure inputs for evacuation or shelter-in-place decisions. Related records: the Newcastle multi-agency incident management digital twin (case_study-newcastle-multi-agency-incident-digital-twin) is a comparable prototype for coordinating ambulance, fire and police.

outcomes: Demonstrates a digital twin that fuses sensor, weather and 3D city data to track and predict urban fire smoke, accounting for building canyon effects and dense populations, with a publicly accessible dashboard for emergency response and public awareness; offered as a replicable framework for municipalities.
